prompt: In 123456789012.dkr.ecr.sa-east-1.amazonaws.com/shop/web:1.0.0, what does sa-east-1 decide?
hint: Each account has one registry per region.

choices.text: The only region where a task may run this image
choices.why: A task in another region may pull it; the pull is slower and the transfer is charged.

choices.text: Which regional registry stores its layers
choices.why: Right. The registry is per account and per region, and the layers live in that region.

choices.text: Nothing: Docker finds the registry from the repository name
choices.why: Docker reads the registry from the part before the first slash, so the hostname is the destination.

choices.text: The region where the image was built, kept as a label
choices.why: Where the build ran is not recorded in the address; the address says where the image is stored.

prompt: A role in account 444455556666 has ecr:BatchGetImage and ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer allowed by its own IAM permissions, and its pulls of shop/web are refused. What is missing?
hint: Two accounts, two halves that have to agree.

choices.text: Tag immutability on your repository
choices.why: Mutability decides whether tags move; it has nothing to do with who may read.

choices.text: Scan on push, which ECR requires before a pull from another account
choices.why: Scanning is about findings, and no pull waits for it.

choices.text: A repository policy that lets 444455556666 in
choices.why: Right. From another account the resource has to allow the caller as well as the caller's own IAM.

choices.text: A KMS key of their own set on your repository
choices.why: Encryption at rest is chosen at creation by the owner, and AES256 does not block another account.

prompt: Whether a repository's layers are encrypted with ECR's key or a KMS key of your own is decided when the repository is ___, and it cannot be changed afterwards.
hint: One moment in the life of a repository.

prompt: aws ecr create-repository --repository-name Shop/Web is refused with InvalidParameterException. Why?
hint: Read the regular expression in the error.

choices.text: A slash is not allowed in a repository name
choices.why: shop/web was created a moment earlier; the slash is part of the name.

choices.text: Capital letters
choices.why: Right. The pattern accepts lowercase letters, digits, and . _ - / between them.

choices.text: The repository Shop has to exist first, as the parent
choices.why: There are no parent repositories: shop/ is a prefix of the name, not a folder.

choices.text: moto refuses a name that AWS would accept
choices.why: moto carries the same expression AWS publishes; AWS refuses it as well.

prompt: A task in the same account pulls shop/web:1.0.0. Which permissions does its role need? Choose all that apply.
hint: One to log in, two to read.

choices.text: ecr:GetAuthorizationToken
choices.why: It produces the token docker login uses.

choices.text: ecr:BatchGetImage
choices.why: It reads the manifest, the first thing a pull fetches.

choices.text: ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer
choices.why: It fetches each layer the manifest names.

choices.text: ecr:PutImage
choices.why: That writes a manifest; a pull reads one.

choices.text: A repository policy naming the account
choices.why: Inside one account, IAM alone decides. The repository policy is for other accounts.

prompt: Put the ECR API calls behind a docker login and docker push in the order they happen.
hint: The manifest names the layers, so it cannot go first.
trap: PutImage is last: the manifest it sends refers to layers the registry has to hold already.

prompt: What is an image's digest?
hint: sha256sum printed it.

choices.text: A random id ECR assigns when a push completes
choices.why: Nothing about it is random: anybody holding the same manifest computes the same digest.

choices.text: The SHA-256 of the biggest layer
choices.why: Each layer has a digest of its own; the image's is computed over the manifest that lists them.

choices.text: The tag, with the registry address in front of it
choices.why: That is the image's name, and a tag moves; a digest does not.

choices.text: The SHA-256 of the manifest's bytes
choices.why: Right. sha256sum manifest.json printed the same value as docker image inspect.

prompt: The lesson's image is 25,988,426 bytes of compressed layers. At 0.10 USD per GB-month, with 1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes, what does storing it cost per month, in USD, to four decimal places?
hint: Bytes over a billion, times the price.

prompt: Against moto, put-image returned a digest different from the one sha256sum manifest.json printed. Which of the two would AWS report for this image?
hint: One of them is computed from the bytes, the other is moto's own arithmetic.

choices.text: The one sha256sum printed
choices.why: Right. AWS hashes the manifest, and docker push reports that same value.

choices.text: The one moto returned, since the registry is what computes it
choices.why: moto derives its value from the list of layer digests; AWS does not.

choices.text: Both, as ECR keeps one digest per tag
choices.why: A digest belongs to the manifest, and two tags on one manifest share it.

choices.text: Neither: AWS digests the config blob rather than the manifest
choices.why: The config has a digest too, listed inside the manifest; the image is named by the manifest's.

prompt: The put-image the lesson ran against moto would be refused by AWS. Why?
hint: What does a push send before the manifest?

choices.text: The manifest was a file, and PutImage accepts manifests from docker alone
choices.why: PutImage accepts any manifest; AWS even documents it for retagging with batch-get-image.

choices.text: None of the layers it names was uploaded (LayersNotFoundException)
choices.why: Right. A manifest may only name layers the repository already holds.

choices.text: The tag 1.0.0 had not been created beforehand
choices.why: Tags are not created separately; PutImage creates the tag.

choices.text: The manifest was not compressed with gzip first
choices.why: Layers travel compressed; the manifest is plain JSON and is sent as it is.

prompt: On AWS, the password aws ecr get-login-password prints is a token that expires after ___ hours.
hint: Half a day.

prompt: In a mutable repository on AWS, 1.0.0 is pushed again with a different image. What becomes of the image 1.0.0 used to name, if it had no other tag?
hint: moto and AWS differ here.

choices.text: It is deleted, as it was in moto
choices.why: That is moto's behaviour. AWS keeps the image.

choices.text: It stays, untagged, still stored and billed
choices.why: Right, and anything that names its digest still pulls it.

choices.text: It keeps the tag, and the new image is refused
choices.why: That is an immutable repository. A mutable one moves the tag.

choices.text: ECR renames its tag to 1.0.0-previous
choices.why: ECR invents no tags; the image simply has none left.

prompt: Match each tag mutability setting to what it allows.
hint: The exclusion list reverses the setting for the tags it matches.

pairs.right: Any tag may be moved to another image
No tag may be moved once pushed
Only tags matching a filter may be moved
Tags matching a filter may not be moved

right_distractors: A tag may move only to a newer image

prompt: A Kubernetes Deployment runs shop/web:1.0.0 with the default pull policy on three nodes. 1.0.0 is overwritten in a mutable repository, and then a fourth node joins and gets a pod. What is running now?
hint: For a tag other than latest, a node pulls only what it does not have.

choices.text: Every pod moves to the new image within a few minutes
choices.why: Nothing tells running pods that the tag moved; they keep the copy their node has.

choices.text: The fourth node refuses to pull a tag that has changed
choices.why: A registry has no notion of a changed tag; it serves whatever the tag names now.

choices.text: The new pod runs the new image and the other three the old one
choices.why: Right: two programs under one version number, and no error anywhere.

choices.text: Four pods on the old image, until somebody edits the Deployment
choices.why: The fourth node had no copy, so it pulled what 1.0.0 names after the overwrite.

prompt: To deploy an image that no later push can change, name it by its ___ instead of a tag: shop/web@sha256: followed by 64 characters.
hint: It is computed from the bytes.

prompt: Under the lesson's lifecycle.json, what happens to an image whose only tag is latest?
hint: Check the three selections against the tag latest.

choices.text: It expires after 7 days, with the untagged images
choices.why: It has a tag, so the untagged rule does not select it.

choices.text: It counts as one of the 30 releases kept
choices.why: latest does not match *.*.*, which needs two dots.

choices.text: It stays: no rule selects it
choices.why: Right. Catching it would take a rule with tagStatus any, read last.

choices.text: It expires after 14 days, like a pull request build
choices.why: That rule matches tags beginning pr-, and latest does not.

prompt: Why does the first rule of lifecycle.json wait seven days before expiring an untagged image, rather than one?
hint: Who else might still be using an image that lost its tag?

choices.text: A deployment pinned to it by digest would fail to pull it
choices.why: Right. Expiring deletes, and a digest names exactly the images a tag left behind.

choices.text: ECR refuses to expire an image younger than seven days
choices.why: There is no such floor; countNumber 1 would expire it after a day.

choices.text: Untagged images are free for their first week
choices.why: Storage is charged from the first day, tagged or not.

choices.text: The preview needs a week of pushes to compute its list
choices.why: A preview evaluates the rules against what is there now.

prompt: Which of these did moto's ECR do in this lesson that AWS would do differently? Choose all that apply.
hint: Compare each with what the prose says AWS does.

choices.text: Deleted an image when its last tag moved away
choices.why: AWS keeps it, untagged.

choices.text: Refused a moved tag with ImageAlreadyExistsException
choices.why: AWS answers ImageTagAlreadyExistsException for a tag in an immutable repository.

choices.text: Failed with an internal error on the lifecycle preview
choices.why: AWS evaluates the rules and lists what they would expire.

choices.text: Refused the repository name Shop/Web
choices.why: AWS refuses it too, with the same regular expression.

choices.text: Kept 1.0.0 in place in the immutable repository
choices.why: That is what AWS does as well.

prompt: Which scan reads the pip packages installed inside an image?
hint: One of the two reads language packages as well.

choices.text: Basic scanning, on every push
choices.why: Basic reads the operating system's packages.

choices.text: Both, the basic one less often
choices.why: The difference is what they read, not only how often.

choices.text: Enhanced scanning, run by Amazon Inspector
choices.why: Right. It reads OS packages and language packages such as pip and npm.

choices.text: Neither: ECR scans the base image and nothing added to it
choices.why: A scan reads the whole image, layers added by your Dockerfile included.

prompt: An image scanned clean on push on Monday. On Wednesday a vulnerability is published in one of its OS packages. With basic scanning, when does the finding appear?
hint: Basic scanning looks at one moment.

choices.text: On Wednesday, when the vulnerability is published
choices.why: Re-scanning on publication is what enhanced scanning adds.

choices.text: When somebody scans that image again
choices.why: Right: on request, at most once every 24 hours for that image.

choices.text: At the next push of any image to the repository
choices.why: Scan on push scans the image being pushed, not the ones already there.

choices.text: Not at all: a basic scan runs once per image, ever
choices.why: A basic scan may be repeated, once per image every 24 hours.

prompt: A repository keeps 40 images of 26 MB each. At 0.10 USD per GB-month, with 1 GB = 1,000 MB, what does it cost per month, in USD?
hint: Images times size, in GB, times the price.

prompt: moto answered the scan with CVE-9999-9999, severity HIGH, in package moto_fake. What does that say about the image?
hint: What did moto ever receive to look inside?

choices.text: It has one high vulnerability, in a package Docker added
choices.why: There is no package by that name, and no such CVE has been published.

choices.text: Nothing: it is a placeholder moto returns for any image
choices.why: Right. moto received a manifest and no layers, so there was nothing to read.

choices.text: Its packages are up to date apart from one
choices.why: moto read no packages at all, so it knows nothing about their versions.

choices.text: That moto reads language packages and not OS packages
choices.why: It reads neither; the finding is the same whatever the image.

prompt: A pipeline pushes ten releases of 26 MB every working day and deletes nothing. After 250 working days, what does the repository cost per month at 0.10 USD per GB-month, with 1 GB = 1,000 MB?
hint: Count the images first.

prompt: Put the steps of publishing shop/web:1.0.1 to ECR and deploying it safely in order.
hint: The name is the destination, and the digest arrives with the push.
items: docker tag it with the repository's address
docker login with the token from aws ecr get-login-password
Deploy it by the digest the push reported
trap: The tag has to come before the push, because docker reads the registry from the name.

prompt: A cluster in us-east-1 pulls shop/web from a repository in sa-east-1 on every new node, and pulls are slow and appear on the bill. What fixes both and keeps one pipeline?
hint: The repository lives in one region.

choices.text: Make the tags immutable
choices.why: Immutability stops tags moving; the layers still cross the continent.

choices.text: A lifecycle policy that keeps fewer images
choices.why: Fewer stored images do not make one pull any shorter.

choices.text: Enhanced scanning turned on in us-east-1
choices.why: Scanning says nothing about where layers are pulled from.

choices.text: Replication of the registry to us-east-1, pulling from there
choices.why: Right. Each push is copied to the other region, and nodes pull from their own.

prompt: Match each error AWS's ECR answers with the situation that produces it.
hint: Read the name of each one closely.

pairs.right: Moving a tag in an immutable repository
The same manifest pushed under the same tag again
A manifest naming layers that were never uploaded
Deleting a repository that still holds images

right_distractors: A tag longer than the repository name
